hero.title: Device Physics and Reliability Across Electronic Platforms.
hero.description: I investigate how interfaces, defects, and electronic and ionic transport govern device operation, variability, and reliability. My research connects physical mechanisms with experimental devices, extending from material and interface engineering to memory arrays, computing hardware, and emerging electronic platforms.

core.title: Memory Device Physics & Reliability
core.description: My core research examines how ionic and defect dynamics govern resistive and analog memory states. I study switching precision, noise, variability, retention, and endurance to connect device physics with reliability.

connected.title: Neuromorphic Computing & Memory Circuits
connected.description: I connect analog device behavior with crossbar arrays, synaptic learning, and CNN inference. Mixed-signal readout, ADC/FPGA-assisted evaluation, and vector–matrix computation extend that work toward memory circuits.
connected.alt: Close view of a patterned microelectronic chip

connected.title: Semiconductor Interfaces & Oxide Electronics
connected.description: My work includes molecular and thin-film interfaces, ALD-based electrodes, oxide electronics, and capacitor structures. I examine charge injection and leakage behavior as foundations for broader semiconductor reliability questions.
connected.alt: Patterned sample held beside laboratory processing equipment

platform.title: Flexible, Stretchable & Optoelectronic Devices
platform.description: I study printed and stretchable interconnects, including electrical variability under deformation. Work on photodetectors and photovoltaic interfaces broadens this device-physics perspective across materials and operating conditions.
platform.alt: Flexible transparent circuit held between gloved hands

outlook.title: Research Outlook
outlook.headline: From Device Physics to Reliable Electronic Systems.
outlook.introduction: I aim to carry insights from interface physics and device experiments into reliable memory and integrated electronic systems.

directions.title: Predictive Memory Reliability
directions.description: Building on ionic memory and interface-controlled transport, I aim to study how defects, noise, leakage, and stress shape memory failure. Future interests include oxide electronics and DRAM-relevant dielectric and capacitor interfaces.

directions.title: Hardware-Aware Memory Computing
directions.description: My work on analog memory, crossbar arrays, and circuit-level evaluation motivates variability-aware hardware and peripheral readout. I am interested in future memory–CMOS co-design.

directions.title: Integrated & Adaptive Electronic Systems
directions.description: Thin-film, optoelectronic, and flexible devices provide a foundation for exploring new architectures. Longer-term interests include low-temperature processing, heterogeneous systems, and three-dimensional integration.
